# procmaps

<!-- badges: start -->

[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html)
[![R build status](https://github.com/r-prof/procmaps/workflows/rcc/badge.svg)](https://github.com/r-prof/procmaps/actions)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/r-prof/procmaps/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/r-prof/procmaps/tree/main)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/procmaps)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=procmaps)
<!-- badges: end -->

The goal of procmaps is to help determine which library or other region is mapped to a specific address of a process.
It is the equivalent of `/proc/self/maps` as a data frame, and is designed to work on all major platforms.

## Goals and non-goals

procmaps aims to:

- Return the address space map of the running process as a data frame, one row per mapped region,
  with the columns `/proc/self/maps` exposes: `from`, `to`, `perms`, `offset`, `inode` and `pathname`.
- Give the same answer on every major platform, including those that have no `/proc/self/maps`,
  by way of the bundled gperftools code.
- Install anywhere without setup: no `./configure` step, no `SystemRequirements`, and no package that must be imported.
- Stay small enough to depend on: two exported functions, `procmap_get()` and `path_is_libr()`.

It is explicitly not trying to:

- Map any process other than the one that calls it.
- Turn an address into a function name or a source location.
  It reports the region an instruction pointer falls into, and the file mapped there.
- Take the backtrace or the profile that produced those instruction pointers in the first place.
- Interpret the map beyond `path_is_libr()`, which matches the basename of R's own library.
- Require tibble: it is used when installed, and `as_tibble = FALSE` always returns a plain data frame.

## Installation

You can install the released version of procmaps from [CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org) with:

``` r
install.packages("procmaps")
```

And the development version from [GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("r-prof/procmaps")
```

## Example

This is what the kernel exposes for this R process on Linux, truncated to its first few regions:

``` r
cat(readLines("/proc/self/maps"), sep = "\n")
```

    56105b1c9000-56105b1ca000 r--p 00000000 fe:00 549660                     /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/bin/exec/R
    56105b1ca000-56105b1cb000 r-xp 00001000 fe:00 549660                     /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/bin/exec/R
    56105b1cb000-56105b1cc000 r--p 00002000 fe:00 549660                     /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/bin/exec/R
    56105b1cc000-56105b1cd000 r--p 00002000 fe:00 549660                     /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/bin/exec/R
    56105b1cd000-56105b1ce000 rw-p 00003000 fe:00 549660                     /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/bin/exec/R
    561096d4b000-56109b491000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [heap]
    7fbd563f2000-7fbd5641c000 r--p 00000000 fe:00 1696201                    /root/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5/testthat/libs/testthat.so
    7fbd5641c000-7fbd5645c000 r-xp 0002a000 fe:00 1696201                    /root/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5/testthat/libs/testthat.so
    7fbd5645c000-7fbd5646f000 r--p 0006a000 fe:00 1696201                    /root/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.5/testthat/libs/testthat.so

Other operating systems make this information available in other form.
This package provides the equivalent as a data frame, regardless of operating system:

``` r
library(procmaps)
procmap_get(as_tibble = TRUE)
```

    #> # A tibble: 530 × 6
    #>    from             to               perms offset   inode   pathname            
    #>    <chr>            <chr>            <chr> <chr>    <chr>   <chr>               
    #>  1 000056105b1c9000 000056105b1ca000 r--p  00000000 549660  /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/…
    #>  2 000056105b1ca000 000056105b1cb000 r-xp  00001000 549660  /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/…
    #>  3 000056105b1cb000 000056105b1cc000 r--p  00002000 549660  /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/…
    #>  4 000056105b1cc000 000056105b1cd000 r--p  00002000 549660  /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/…
    #>  5 000056105b1cd000 000056105b1ce000 rw-p  00003000 549660  /opt/R/4.5.3/lib/R/…
    #>  6 0000561096d4b000 000056109b6f2000 rw-p  00000000 0       [heap]              
    #>  7 00007fbd563f2000 00007fbd5641c000 r--p  00000000 1696201 /root/R/x86_64-pc-l…
    #>  8 00007fbd5641c000 00007fbd5645c000 r-xp  0002a000 1696201 /root/R/x86_64-pc-l…
    #>  9 00007fbd5645c000 00007fbd5646f000 r--p  0006a000 1696201 /root/R/x86_64-pc-l…
    #> 10 00007fbd5646f000 00007fbd56473000 r--p  0007c000 1696201 /root/R/x86_64-pc-l…
    #> # ℹ 520 more rows

Both outputs above are recordings of the same R process, taken on x86_64 Linux under R 4.5.3 and replayed from `README-fixtures/`,
so the addresses in the two views correspond.
The one exception is `[heap]`, which ends higher in the second view,
because `procmap_get()` allocates between the two snapshots and the heap grows.
A live run would differ on every render, because the addresses are randomised and the mapped regions depend on the machine.
